ops.title: Sparse Mac launch waits on Orca's five-minute worktree rescan
ops.premise:
Premise: a sparse Mac launch (`ORCA_LAUNCH_SPARSE=1`) adds its worktree with plain `git worktree add --no-checkout` (lr `addSparseWorktree`), and Orca 1.4.247 lists that path only on its next periodic rescan of the repo, so `listedWorktree` can exceed its `l.stall + 300` s budget and fail the launch with `LAUNCH-FAILED: Orca does not list worktree ... yet` (11 in 24 h, cci 540421 et al.).

How Orca's runtime learns about worktrees (read from /Applications/Orca.app 1.4.247, out/main/index.js, extracted from app.asar):
- Every selector form (`path:`, `id:<repo-id>::<path>`, `name:`, `branch:`) resolves against rows built by `d3` -> `Vdr` -> `scanRepo` -> `listRepoWorktreesForResolution`. `resolveExplicitWorktreeIdScoped` (`Wdr`) for `id:` also calls `d3`, so it reads the same cache; no selector bypasses it.
- `listRepoWorktreesForResolution` keeps a per-repo scan cache: entries live `PPr` = 30 s (300 s only for paths under .codex-tmp, .codex/vendor_imports, .claude/skills). On expiry `refreshRepoWorktreeScan` probes an "admin fingerprint" of `<common>/.git/worktrees/*` (gitdir, HEAD, ref, locked, packed-refs). If the probe is still pending, or misses its `Xdr` = 3.5 s budget, it logs "[worktree-scan] admin fingerprint unknown; reusing cached rows until the reconcile ceiling" and returns the cached rows until 300 s (`3e5`) after the last real scan. `Vdr` also caps the whole scan at 5 s and falls back to stored metadata rows, which a plain-git worktree does not have yet.
- Nothing watches `.git/worktrees`. The scan generation is bumped (forcing an immediate `git worktree list`) only by `Uo(repoId)` -> `invalidateWorktreeCatalog`, which Orca calls from its own worktree create and remove, from `worktree set` when it changes metadata on an already-resolved worktree, and from branch or folder renames. `orca repo set` notifies with `invalidateGitScans:false`.
- The CLI has no verb that adopts or registers an existing path: no adopt, import, or refresh in `orca agent-context --json` (284 KB schema) or `orca skills get orca-cli`. `adoptManagedProvisionedRoot` exists for environment recipes only and refuses sparse checkouts.
- The runtime's create already supports sparse worktrees: shared/rpc-contract/worktree-create-params.js carries `sparseCheckout: {directories, presetId}`, and the create path (`sjr`/`ljr`) checks out sparse and records `sparseDirectories`. The CLI `orca worktree create` exposes no flag for it.

Evidence:
- Orca records every git exec that fails or takes >= 250 ms (runner chunk `Gn`, `In=250`). Every `git worktree list` on /Users/yasyf/Code/monorepo (1,494 entries in .git/worktrees) takes 311-1,335 ms, so all of them are in ~/Library/Application Support/orca/logs/main.trace.ndjson*. From 06:48:59 to 07:54:11 PT Nov 6 there were 16, at gaps of 51-402 s, median 311 s: Orca rescans this repo about every five minutes despite lanes adding worktrees continuously.
- A replica of the fingerprint probe over the same 1,494 entries finishes in 81-100 ms in a fresh Node process, so the probe's own I/O is not what exceeds 3.5 s. Why it misses inside Orca's main process is not proven.
- `orca worktree show --worktree path:/Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/monorepo/monorepo/dar-sentry-7832942245-evidence-f77854b1-1 --json` answers ok minutes after the launch saved `selector_not_found` (brief).
- lr #3361 (59ae1816f) already lengthened the wait to `l.stall + worktreeCacheSeconds` (300 s); the five-minute reconcile ceiling plus scan jitter still exceeds it.

Root cause: lr creates the sparse worktree behind Orca's back, and Orca 1.4.247 offers no CLI call that registers an existing worktree path or invalidates the repo's scan cache, so the path becomes visible only on Orca's roughly five-minute reconcile.
